The above function $F(x)$ is defined on $x\in [-3,3).$ Let $f(x)$ be the $6$-periodic extension of $F(x)$ to $x\in R.$
Select the correct options below.

| I. | $F(x)$ is continuous on $x\in (-3,3)$ | {{field-1}} |
| --- | --- | --- |
| II. | $F(x)$ is piecewise smooth on $x\in (-3,3)$ | {{field-2}} |
| III. | ${lim}_{x\to -{3}^{+}}F(x)={lim}_{x\to {3}^{-}}F(x)$ | {{field-3}} |
| IV. | $f(x)$ is piecewise smooth and continuous on $R$ | {{field-4}} |

The above function $F(x)$ is defined on $x \in [-2,2).$ Let $f(x)$ be the $4$-periodic extension of $F(x)$ to $x\in\mathbb{R}.$
Determine whether each statement below is true or false.

- $F(x)$ is continuous on $x\in(-2,2).$

- $F(x)$ is piecewise smooth on $x\in(-2,2).$

- $\lim\limits_{x \to -2^+} F(x) = \lim\limits_{x \to 2^-} F(x).$

- $f(x)$ is piecewise smooth and continuous on $\mathbb{R}.$
examples.worked_solution:
Let's examine the given statements in turn.

- Statement I is true. The function $F(x)$ is continuous on $x \in (-2,2).$ Its graph is shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14069003/assets/5c1cc57825a318df088ac0bc28ffe75c21579c5fe007fbb52cf0710a1937dc1e.png)

- Statement II is true. The function $F(x)$ is piecewise smooth on $x \in (-2,2).$ It consists of two smooth pieces.

- Statement III is true. Indeed, we have

$$
\lim\limits_{x \to -2^+} F(x) = \lim\limits_{x \to -2^+} (-2x) = -2(-2) = 4
$$

and 

$$
\lim\limits_{x \to 2^-} F(x) = \lim\limits_{x \to 2^-} x^2 = (2)^2 = 4.
$$

So, $\lim\limits_{x \to -2^+} F(x) = \lim\limits_{x \to 2^-} F(x).$

- Statement IV is true since statements I, II, and III are all true.

**Note:** The $4$-periodic extension of $F(x)$ to $x \in \mathbb{R}$ has the graph shown below.
